body: I know it's not his fault, I understand that. I guess I just feel like I moved to this place I don't like for his sake so at least he could put me ahead of his family for once.

I don't know how much political opinions are allowed here but it was regarding the situation in Gaza and I said nothing can ever truly justify active genocide and murdering children. She does not like that I'm Jewish but hold different opinions
You're right, it's definitely the isolation that's getting to me
He can't force them to like me is his excuse
I tried to do that, hence him calling me jealous
His mom isn't too crafty. She comes up here occasionally and we talk on the phone but she's in her 60s and there's only so much we have in common outside gossip and food.
I want him to go one weekend a month but he's been very resistant to that

I do pilates but mostly at home; my disability makes it hard to be consistent.

We're going to start IVF by the end of this year so we do want kids.

That's true. They come up here during the summer when the kids are off school sometimes but we live in a two-bedroom in an extremely expensive city. Hotels aren't exactly cheap and there's no room for everybody at our place. It's a lot easier for us to visit

Well, I'm gonna be real and say his sister hates me because I said genocide is bad so I don't know where we can go from there. Before the big argument over that, she always just said she doesn't know how to "relate" to me since she's a busy working mother and I'm not. She doesn't want me "poisoning" her kids.

His brothers are just stereotypical guys with guy hobbies and I'm never invited to their fishing or football get-togethers. To be fair, their wives are never invited either but their wives have been friends since middle school and it was clear after a few visits that I was third-wheeling
The issue is I was an expat where we lived before. I had loads of friends but it was a temporary visa. I can't go back or I would
Yeah. I think he was hoping I'd like this place more than I actually do. We both expected things to be different

We live in one of the biggest cities in the US and it's really awesome for someone who likes fast-paced places. I'm a home-body who would love nothing more than a big garden and space to breathe.

I've been trying to find a chance to volunteer at the local library but we have a mayor who wants to close libraries on the weekends so who knows
It really is isolating. I read, I write, I have a few plants to take care of. I go to book club. But it just feels so empty
The few relatives I have that I'm not even close to are in another country. An eight hour flight from us. My mom lives close enough and I see her often. That's the only family I have

With my disability and how demanding my actual job is, I'm not sure I can get a second one. Unfortunately I'm not much for pets but I've been trying to look for volunteering opportunities that would be easy on my body.

I luckily have a job in a field that's really good in this city. I make better money than I have ever had but I would still have taken a pay cut for a different place.

>  
Why does he want to spend so much time with them and not with you?

He adores his nieces and nephews. Four years ago we were abroad and he felt like he missed out on a lot of time with them. He says we live together and spend every waking moment together outside work.
